prayerExcerpt.en-US: "I was called to tell this story. I never tire of telling it. I love my calling."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: "Fui chamado para contar esta história. Nunca me canso de contá-la. Amo o meu chamado."

meta.face: An American of Irish stock of about sixty with a fair complexion and a LONG, LEAN face with HIGH, sharply MODELLED cheekbones and hollowed cheeks — a high forehead under dark, wavy hair greying at the temples, brushed back from a slight widow's peak under the zucchetto, strong, ARCHED dark brows, LARGE, light, deep-set, INTENSE eyes that seem to look straight through the viewer, a long, straight nose, deep lines from the nose to a WIDE, thin-lipped mouth in a warm, slightly lifted smile, and a firm, narrow chin; the gaze magnetic and kind. Not the square-chinned, level-browed giovanni_battista_scalabrini, nor the white-haired, laughing giuseppe_allamano.
meta.basis: His photographs (Wikimedia Commons: the New York World-Telegram photograph of 1952 in cape and pectoral cross; the ABC photograph of 1956; the Library of Congress portraits as a young priest; the Dicastery's portrait): a long, lean face with high cheekbones, dark wavy hair brushed back, arched brows over large, intense, deep-set eyes, and a wide, thin smile, in the bishop's cassock, zucchetto and cape. Wikipedia records his burial at St. Patrick's Cathedral, New York (moved to Peoria in 2019), where he preached for years.
meta.excerpt: His answer to a friend who asked why he became a priest, «I was called to tell this story (the Gospel). I never tire of telling it. I never tire of improving my telling of it. I love my calling», as Cardinal Tagle quoted it in the beatification homily of 24 September 2026 (on the Dicastery's page; also Vatican News); a single short quotation, shortened, the gloss and the third sentence left out; pt-BR our rendering
